Topics · Meaning and purpose

What do I owe the poor?

A short chapter ties religion to the orphan and needy, and giving what we love sits at the heart of goodness.

Part 1 of 3

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ أَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى يُكَذِّبُ بِٱلدِّينِ١ فَذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِى يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ٢ وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? For that is the one who drives away the orphan And does not encourage the feeding of the poor.

Quran · Al-Ma'un 107:1-3

Translation

But you do see trouble and grief. You consider it to take it into your hand. You help the victim and the fatherless.

Original · Hebrew

רָאִ֡תָה כִּֽי־אַתָּ֤ה ׀ עָ֘מָ֤ל וָכַ֨עַס ׀ תַּבִּיט֮ לָתֵ֪ת בְּיָ֫דֶ֥ךָ עָ֭לֶיךָ יַעֲזֹ֣ב חֵלֶ֑כָה יָ֝ת֗וֹם אַתָּ֤ה ׀ הָיִ֬יתָ עוֹזֵֽר׃

the Psalms · 10:14

World English Bible

How can you tell what someone truly believes? Less from their words than from how they treat one who can give nothing back. The verses ask: have you seen the one who denies the religion? You expect an intellectual description, and something else comes: he pushes the orphan away, and does not urge others to feed the needy. Here a person's tie to religion is known at the table before it is known in debate.

A question for you

What did you expect the verses to describe?

If you sayA man who denies God.
ThenThat is what makes the description a surprise: the verses go straight to the table.
If you sayA hard-hearted man.
ThenThen the verses arrive where you already were.
If you sayI did not expect anything.
ThenThen this description may stay with you longer.

Part 2 of 3

﴿لَّيْسَ ٱلْبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ قِبَلَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلْبِرَّ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْـَٔاخِرِ وَٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلْكِتَـٰبِ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَءَاتَى ٱلْمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ ذَوِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْيَتَـٰمَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَـٰكِينَ وَٱبْنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَٱلسَّآئِلِينَ وَفِى ٱلرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلْمُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِهِمْ إِذَا عَـٰهَدُوا۟ ۖ وَٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ فِى ٱلْبَأْسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَحِينَ ٱلْبَأْسِ ۗ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا۟ ۖ وَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but [true] righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allāh, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets and gives wealth, in spite of love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask [for help], and for freeing slaves; [and who] establishes prayer and gives zakāh; [those who] fulfill their promise when they promise; and [those who] are patient in poverty and hardship and during battle. Those are the ones who have been true, and it is those who are the righteous.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:177

Translation

If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also. Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two. Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.

Original · Ancient Greek

καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν, ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον· καὶ ὅστις σε ἀγγαρεύσει μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετʼ αὐτοῦ δύο. τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δός, καὶ τὸν θέλοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ δανίσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῇς.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 5:40-42

World English Bible

It is easy to give what you do not need. The verse asks something harder. Goodness is not turning east or west; it is faith in God and the Last Day, and giving wealth despite loving it: to kin, orphans, the needy, the traveller. Giving what you love is what tests the heart. The verse joins faith and deed in one sentence, and calls such people truthful.

A question for you

Which group in the verse is usually farthest from your mind?

If you sayMy own kin.
ThenPerhaps those nearest are the hardest. The list starts with them.
If you sayThe traveller.
ThenThe stranger cut off from home. There are many in today's world.
If you sayThe needy.
ThenThey may be close by and unseen. The Step begins there.

Part 3 of 3

﴿ٱلَّذِى يُؤْتِى مَالَهُۥ يَتَزَكَّىٰ١٨ وَمَا لِأَحَدٍ عِندَهُۥ مِن نِّعْمَةٍ تُجْزَىٰٓ١٩ إِلَّا ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ٢٠﴾

Translation of the meaning

[He] who gives [from] his wealth to purify himself And not [giving] for anyone who has [done him] a favor to be rewarded[1939] – But only seeking the face [i.e., acceptance] of his Lord, Most High.

Translator's notes

[1939] i.e., without intending reciprocation for some benefit to himself.

Quran · Al-Layl 92:18-20

Translation

But give for gifts to the needy those things which are within, and behold, all things will be clean to you.

Original · Ancient Greek

πλὴν τὰ ἐνόντα δότε ἐλεημοσύνην, καὶ ἰδοὺ πάντα καθαρὰ ὑμῖν ἐστιν.

the Gospel (Luke) · 11:41

World English Bible

﴿إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنكُمْ جَزَآءً وَلَا شُكُورًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

[Saying], "We feed you only for the face [i.e., approval] of Allāh. We wish not from you reward or gratitude.

Quran · Al-Insan 76:9

Translation

It is well with the man who deals graciously and lends. He will maintain his cause in judgment. For he will never be shaken. The righteous will be remembered forever. He will not be afraid of evil news. His heart is steadfast, trusting in Yahweh. His heart is established. He will not be afraid in the end when he sees his adversaries. He has dispersed, he has given to the poor. His righteousness endures forever. His horn will be exalted with honor.

Original · Hebrew

טֽוֹב־אִ֭ישׁ חוֹנֵ֣ן וּמַלְוֶ֑ה יְכַלְכֵּ֖ל דְּבָרָ֣יו בְּמִשְׁפָּֽט׃ כִּֽי־לְעוֹלָ֥ם לֹא־יִמּ֑וֹט לְזֵ֥כֶר ע֝וֹלָ֗ם יִהְיֶ֥ה צַדִּֽיק׃ מִשְּׁמוּעָ֣ה רָ֭עָה לֹ֣א יִירָ֑א נָכ֥וֹן לִ֝בּ֗וֹ בָּטֻ֥חַ בַּיהוָֽה׃ סָמ֣וּךְ לִ֭בּוֹ לֹ֣א יִירָ֑א עַ֖ד אֲשֶׁר־יִרְאֶ֣ה בְצָרָֽיו׃ פִּזַּ֤ר ׀ נָ֘תַ֤ן לָאֶבְיוֹנִ֗ים צִ֭דְקָתוֹ עֹמֶ֣דֶת לָעַ֑ד קַ֝רְנ֗וֹ תָּר֥וּם בְּכָבֽוֹד׃

the Psalms · 112:5-9

World English Bible

If you give in order to be thanked, you have already taken your payment. These verses say the one who gives to grow purer owes no one a favour in return, and seeks only the face of their Lord. Those who feed others say: we want no reward or thanks from you. So the poor owe you nothing. They are not shamed or reminded. What you owe the poor begins with money, and is complete when they feel no debt.

A question for you

When is giving hardest for you?

If you sayWhen no one thanks me.
ThenAn honest admission, and the verses speak to it directly.
If you sayWhen I worry what is left will not be enough.
ThenAn understandable worry. The verses do not ask you to ruin yourself, and 2:286 sets the charge at capacity.
If you sayWhen I do not know if it will reach those in need.
ThenA fair practical question. Taking care does not lessen what you do.

The same in the other books

Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτὸν ταῦτα ἐπάρασά τις φωνὴν γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακαρία ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασά σε καὶ μαστοὶ οὓς ἐθήλασας· αὐτὸς δὲ εἶπεν· Μενοῦν μακάριοι οἱ ἀκούοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ φυλάσσοντες.

the Gospel (Luke) · 11:27-28

World English Bible

Translation

Tear your heart and not your garments, and turn to Yahweh, your God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and relents from sending calamity.

Original · Hebrew

וְקִרְע֤וּ לְבַבְכֶם֙ וְאַל־בִּגְדֵיכֶ֔ם וְשׁ֖וּבוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־חַנּ֤וּן וְרַחוּם֙ ה֔וּא אֶ֤רֶךְ אַפַּ֨יִם֙ וְרַב־חֶ֔סֶד וְנִחָ֖ם עַל־הָרָעָֽה׃
